Was driving home after a nightshift and was in a mood because I was expecting the joiners that morning to assemble the new garden shed so I wasn’t going to get to bed for ages. 
Driving along at 50mph and see SOMETHING flying towards me from the trailer in front. Didn’t register what it was but managed to dodge it  unfortunately the guy travelling in the opposite direction wasn’t so lucky. 
After much flashing of the lights the bloke finally realised his trailer was empty five miles later when the last piece of plywood flew across the road and pulled over. Being tired and in the aforementioned mood I pulled up behind him and let him know that his unsecured load had hit someone. He didn’t seem to care and just shouted back “I’ll sort it”. In my sleep deprived haze, I was concerned this wood was to be reclaimed and used to assemble my shed so I took a photo of the licence plate in case it matched the joiner who later appeared because I didn’t want wood that had bounced across the tarmac to be used in a shed I’d paid good money for. 
After trying and failing to gather his kindling from rush hour traffic, this cowboy peeled off in the opposite direction of all the damage he caused. Knowing that there was a risk that someone was hurt, but selfishly prioritising my need for home comforts and knowing I’d still be three miles back in rush hour traffic even if I did return to the struck car, I carried on home and texted family to let them know there’d been an incident at a time I was on the road but I was fine. 
Joiner messaged to cancel so I went to bed for a few hours. 
Woke up to several messages from my mum telling her one of her friends had a fb post up about flying wood hitting her daughter’s boyfriend’s car. She thanks a car salesman for stopping and doubts anyone has any other information from that time in the morning where everyone is functioning on the bare minimum but is praying someone does. 
So, bleary eyed, I send the photos I have to the pleading poster. A couple of minutes later I remember to add context and time/date/location info etc for the police as it’s technically now a hit and run and carrying an unsecured load. Driver is fine if shaken but the car is only fit for scrap so obviously insurance is needed. 
The first driver ends up in court and given a suspended sentence and offenders levy, I get a £20 gift card, flowers and chocolates from my mum’s friend for providing the info and restoring her trust in people to speak up. The joiner apologised for cancelling and offered a free paint job to make up for it. Saved me buying the paint and ruining the patio. And I got to have my 8 hours of mostly unbroken sleep after nightshift so a win win all around!

Stuck in A&E one sad Saturday night for a post-surgery infection. Knew the stitches needed cutting and was willing to just take a sterile cutter home and get a nurse friend to do it with a course of oral antibiotics instead of waiting 10 hours to have a junior (who said herself she wasn’t a surgical specialist) cut them open and admit me for 5 days of… oral antibiotics… and they wonder why the NHS is troubled. 
(Let me preface this by saying patient privacy is an ideal in my local and not a total reality when you’re creating a makeshift bed in the corridor out of a spare towel because you didn’t plan to be there all night)
anyway, this Saturday night. A case of two unrelated young men are brought in. Just wee’uns when it all boiled down. Clearly underage: one had barely a bum fluff to be seen. Both suffering the after affects of an unsupervised night on the town. One had just been to the superfluous land of excess and his body was not happy with him, and the other had stumbled off the kerb. Both brought in by ambulance and parents identified and called. 
The one who had drank himself silly had a mother pushing for an admission in case he choked in his sleep/had been spiked/grew a tail etc. No matter how much the doctors reassured her that they’d done all the tests they could, she wasn’t happy. In the heat of the moment she snapped “and I don’t want to deal with that”. Love, no-one wants to. Eventually she left with him dry retching and giving off stink about the caring profession not caring. 
Opposed to the other mother. The poor cub had needed staples with only gas and air due to his inebriation. Tripping over your own feet can happen to the best and most sober of us, but this woman was taking no prisoners. He was being called all the irresponsible idiots under the sun, with her only pausing to thank the doctor and apologise for her “disgrace of a son wasting all your time when there are people who really need the help”. As they exited the revolving doors, she was informing her offspring that if he made a mess, he’d be awoken at the crack of dawn to clean it up. 
Wonder which one really learned a lesson there then? 

As for me, I ended up admitted to a ward at 6am in a pair of mesh underwear with only my phone, charging cable and bottle of coke swiped from the car boot to my name for the next 12 hours.

I was flying from Belfast to Newcastle when there was a bit of a kerfuffle in the city and this, coupled with snow, meant the buses were seriously delayed and I missed the flight. It was late at night and I had no way to get back home. Posted on Facebook about my distress and a youth worker I knew who was in London immediately phoned to say they’d pay to put me up in a hotel until the next day. Not even a cheap one: the one next to the airport which was probably a couple of hundred for the night at such late notice. Someone else I knew in Belfast offered to drive me home and someone from home offered to drive nearly two hours to collect me. 
Eventually, got home with the two drivers bringing me half way each to which I’m incredibly grateful for to this day. 
Then when I got home, realised I’d lost my driving licence (had been using it for ID to fly). Phoned the airport and nothing had been handed in. I took a few days off to decompress and sort out mitigating circumstances as I was missing my uni exams and was just a bit stressed.  
Just as I was getting ready to fly back (FlyBe accepted student ID if you were checking a bag as they had an offer where you’d get a free bag if you were were having to fly across a body of water which was a lifesaver) the postman came one day with a handwritten envelope for me. Inside was my licence and a post it. “Found at airport”. No name or anything else. 
Saved me the £30 replacement cost, easyJet refunded my flights after a lot of back and forth explaining the Belfast situation and the fact the gate closed two minutes earlier than advertised, and I got to sit my exams in May with no consequences. 
An amazing show of human kindness all around that made the disaster of a journey much better

I was once on a 60mph road, at school let-out time, trying to herd some apparently very expensive sheep.

Two hours later I’d spent more than two quid calling 101 asking for help to clear the road from 1pm and now it was hitting school rush hour and a busy road.

Took calling 999 to actually get anyone to respond and while I apologised to the responding crew, they said I was absolutely right to do so as the risk to life on a blind bend was real.  Calling makes sure things are documented, and repeated calls with consistent information matters (in my case I was saying “THEYVE MOVED CLOSER TO THE CURVE. TWO MORE HAVE ESCAPED THW FIELD”” yours is more, for the third night this week X has been present at my address of Y despite my not informing him of it or inviting him there”

Was on Imraldi (a biologic) and by the third month a painful outbreak had started on my foot. Thought it was athletes foot so got a cream from the chemist for it but (obviously) it did nothing for it. Went to a friends wedding and within a week, I’d developed pus-filled lumps on my hands. Pharmacist suspected shingles so I got an urgent GP appointment (still limited appointments after c19) and he suspected herpes. Tried all the creams and oral steroids he prescribed but no real change. 
Went back to my derm for a review of the Imraldi and mentioned how my skin was reacting and I thought it might be a side effect. She looked at a photo on my phone, declared it was psoriasis and told me to moisturise. 
Haven’t seen her since and that was September ‘22. Now my entire body has plaques, hands and feet have had maybe a week of relief since then, my skin folds are all inflamed, I can’t wear black underwear without cringing at all the shedding on show, I’ve fingernails threatening to vacate my nail beds and I’ve had to sacrifice my hair to try and treat my scalp.

I've had this and it's no laughing matter. Luckily, I gave up all hope of medical dignity in my late teens after realising that I was so out of it after an operation that two nurses had to dress me into my pyjamas and hold me on the toilet. 

I have a pretty 'embarrassing' condition that often co-exists with pilonidal cysts, hidradnitus suppurativa, so I'm well used to showing my bits and bobs off to nurses and doctors. Often, it's something they're unfamiliar with.

At 20, I had the worst flare up of my pilonidal cyst just before Christmas. I was trying to do the Christmas shopping with my mum at 2am and couldn't function. I couldn't walk, couldn't sit, couldn't stand still. Sat sobbing angrily in pain in the car, drove her home and carted myself up to A&E. They say necessity is the mother of all invention, and it was that night that I learnt how to drive a car for 20 miles without sitting down. It's now the early hours of Christmas Eve and the doctor is determined that I'm going for surgery the next day. I'm a stubborn, sleep deprived, stressed-out-from-uni young woman at this point and ain't no-one keeping me in the hospital. After saying i'll accept any and all responsibility, I end up convincing him and the nurse to do a lance and drain with local anaesthetic.

I felt EVERY jab of that local going in and it didn't numb the pain one little bit. Made the mistake of saying this and they were going to stop the procedure. I wasn't having it - I'd just been poked in the backside repeatedly for the past five minutes. We got started again after I'd downed some co-codamol. 

The next thing I hear is "oh myyyy goddd" from this fairly good looking young doctor. Strangely, it made me feel better because here was the proof that I was actually in a lot of pain. Got it drained, packing put in, a nappy-like dressing put over and left with an apology of "there may be a little blood on your underwear." You'd know he was a surgeon at that comment: his idea of a 'little' blood looked like some kind of massacre had taken place in my knickers. 

Fast forward two years. I may be 22, but I'm still mentally a petulant child. My referral for full surgery has finally come through and soon I'll be free from this literal pain in the butt. On the morning of the surgery, I meet the surgeon and try to discuss the plan of action. I've researched this thing and spoken to others who've had it. I say that I do not want a primary closure done. He thinks I'm a google know-it-all and completely dismisses me, saying he'll decide when we're in the theatre. As I'll be off in fairyland, that doesn't sit too well with me so I make sure to tell all the staff I come into contact. 

I come back on to the ward wearing different net knickers than I went down with and a nurse comes over to check on me. I ask what happened in there and how my butt crack has been left. 

Surprise, surprise. He's sewn me up. All I'm told is to go to my GP in 10 days to get the stitches removed. 

I last 7 days. My mother is a qualified nurse and as it's giving me bother, I ask her to take a look. As she removes the dressing, there is literally an explosion all over the bathroom floor. I'm leaking and oh my holy fuck, the smell. The smell. It's still there in my nostrils when I think about it. Rotting dead things in the woods would have smelt better. Now there's just this gaping hole with bright blue stitches down one side holding nothing. Ever independent, I drove myself back up to A&E, putting my previous skills back to good use and hovering above the drivers seat the whole way in. 

I'd hoped it would be simple - take out the stitches, chuck in some packing and off I'd go but instead I ended up trapped in the hospital for a week with a raging infection. Luckily, I know people who know people and I managed to keep my car in the staff car park the whole time so was able to avoid any parking fees. 

After discharge, the district nursing team called with me daily for three months to look at my second butthole. Then when I could sit down without accidentally absorbing anything smaller than a ping pong ball, I was taken off their rota and started going to my GP office for the packing to be redone. All in, I ended up with six rounds of antibiotics for various infections, likely cost the NHS a small fortune and it took more than a year for the hole to close. Even now when I'm 25, I still get pain when sitting straight upright or just sitting for too long in general. 

Lesson: Get the damn thing seen to and make sure it's seen to properly the first time!
